findings.title: The empty-expr filter now runs before interpolation, so queries that interpolate to an empty string are no longer dropped.
findings.body:
The old code interpolated first (`interpolateVariablesInQueries`) and then dropped targets with an empty `expr`. The new code checks `query.expr` on the raw text and only then calls `applyTemplateVariables`.

**Trigger:** a target whose expr is just a variable, such as `$query`, and that variable resolves to an empty value.

**What goes wrong:** the raw text `$query` passes the filter, interpolation turns it into `""`, and the empty query goes on to `splitQueriesByStreamShard`. There it is used to fetch shard values and is sent to Loki, which returns a parse error. Before this change the query was skipped.

**Fix:** interpolate first, then filter on the interpolated expr.

held.title: Interpolating before `querySupportsSplitting` may hide `$__range` from the guard that stops those queries from being split.
held.body:
`querySupportsSplitting` uses `isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr)` to keep queries that use `$__range`, `$__range_s` or `$__range_ms` out of splitting. The backend has to fill those in with each chunk's own time range. Now `applyTemplateVariables` runs before the partition, so the guard sees the interpolated expression. If `templateSrv.replace` or the request's `scopedVars` fill in `$__range` on the frontend, the guard no longer finds the variable. The query then gets split, and every chunk uses the full dashboard range instead of the chunk range, so a normal `[$__range]` query returns wrong results.

I couldn't check whether the frontend interpolator fills in `$__range` for Loki requests. If it can, run the `nonSplittingQueries` partition on the raw targets and interpolate only after that, or check `isQueryWithRangeVariable` against the original expression.
